title: Is This Tyler Huntley's Best Stretch as a Raven?
text: You need to get them back to 100%, because I don't want to spend another 3 months with persistent injuries. Well, Jeff, how about Tyler Huntley in a bind once again, in his third stint in Baltimore?  This time, in the last quarter and overtime.  Is that the most impressive stretch we 've seen from him, including the one in Green Bay ? Was last year a crucial moment, but this time the stakes are higher?  No, they had to win that game against the Packers to stay in the playoff hunt last year, but my God, he had such dominance that we could all see it, the prime- time audience could see it on Sunday night. Yes, I think that when Tyler Huntley is at his best, we all said it and wrote this, he manages the game in the past.  Perhaps, you know , they're running well with the ball and supporting it.  You really don't have to do much.  First read, release the ball quickly, short passes, hold onto it and run if the first option is covered, and simply leave the game in the hands of Derrick Henry.  When you're losing by eight points with 2:25 left and you're on your own...is it the 20-yard line or the 10-yard line after the 10- yard penalty?  You can't do that.  That game was on Tyler Huntley's shoulders and he had to go out and win it, and that's exactly what he did.  I...there simply isn't a happier, more professional guy in that locker room.  Everyone wants it.    He's always ready.  He never complains.  That's why , you know, I think we can get a little defensive about the criticism directed at him and people, you know, wanting him to be immediately discarded in favor of an undrafted rookie quarterback who played a couple of good preseason games. This guy has won in the NFL.  He has won important matches.  It has given us the opportunity to beat really good teams, even in matches we have lost.  And I think you have to give him a lot of credit, man.  And he's not , you know, he never looks good. There are always aspects where, you know, it takes on a frantic appearance where, you know, he taps the ball, walks on his toes a bit, he just doesn't seem comfortable.  But then you look at the end and when he has to be at his best, he has typically been able to rise to the occasion and perform at his best. Hopefully, this will give him the credit he deserves.  I don't know if people understand how valuable it is to have a guy earning $2.5 million on your staff.  He is the 49th highest-paid quarterback in the NFL this year.  He's a mid-level backup quarterback's salary and still has a .500 record with the Ravens. And a backup quarterback with a .500 record in the NFL is a great asset.  It's a great phrase to put on your resume as a backup quarterback. They trust him, they believe in him, and when they need him, he has almost always delivered. So this was huge, you know, they're heading into the toughest stretch of the season.  We all know it.  This was a great victory and yes, Derrick Henry helped.  Yes, Kyle Hamilton closed the deal.  All those things.  Bateman and Zay and the great plays of Justice Hill. But he led that team and made plays when it was necessary.  It wasn't Derrick Henry who led them all over the field.  He was on the bench for most of that series to tie the game because they were in 2-minute mode.  So, give him all the credit he deserves.  He deserves it this week and people are very happy for him, because he's a guy who does things right, he's down-to-earth, never asks for much and is always ready to play. Barry, I want to thank PrizePicks, America's number one sports prediction app .  They have been with us throughout 2026. They will continue to be one of our main sponsors.  They can use the code HMA and new users play five dollars.  If they do, they will get $150 when they win. Any predictions for week six, guys?  Kenneth Walker III scored over half a touchdown at any time against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.  JSN against the Denver Broncos, more than six and a half receptions.  And the king in Cleveland, more than half a touchdown at any moment.  Go ahead and send those forecasts.  We've been tracking our bets all year long. We will continue to do so by sending that lineup.  And again, at prizepicks.com, we hope you'll use our code.  They really support the program and they have supported us, which we appreciate. Yes, I want to give some opinions about Huntley.  First, I think something I noticed was that he operates better from an open shotgun formation, because that's what we saw not only in the series to tie the game, but also in the overtime series. I think Greg Roman came on in that game in the first half and really wanted to play from under the center to try and develop the play-action game, which makes sense.  You're going to use your backup quarterback.  As Jeff said, you want to manage the game, put it in game management mode, lean into your ground game, set up the action game , all those good things.  I simply do n't think that's Tyler Huntley's style of play.  I think it processes information well and it showed.  As there were two specific plays in the winning offensive series, both on third downs.  The first was the quick pass to Mark Andrews on third and six.  He threw that straight into the blitz, perfectly placed. He saw it before the serve, he saw that blitz coming.  As soon as the serve was made, he saw Mark turn.  Good move by Mark. We'll talk about Mark later.  There's a lot to say there.  But that was a veteran play by Mark, simply knowing that the defender marking him came out to pressure him and managing to get to the first down mark.  And then, on the next third chance, he finds Zay Flowers.  And then, you know, it got me thinking that it's not like you want to completely change your offense , but I think if they want Tyler Huntley to work, if he comes in as a starter this week, I think maybe go back to some of the success they had with that 3-for-1 shotgun formation, 11-man personnel, empty formation, with fewer tight ends.  I think that's what I'd like to see, especially if Matt Hibner is dealing with some hand injuries.  I don't know how much they want to use Kway Voss and Vinnett, but that's one conclusion I would draw from Tyler Huntley's performance .  Number two, I think Rashod Bateman deserves a lot of credit.  He had about three receptions for 37 yards on that series that tied the game and ended with Tez Walker's touchdown . They achieved four out of 43 in their last two series overall. That's where the key lay.  Yes, those were simply impressive plays.  He played like a true veteran.  It's one of those things where you need the guys to step up and make plays, and the yards after the catch he got, I think they led to Tez Walker's touchdown actually.    It was simply a beautiful play.  And again, you can see Tyler Huntley's processing power.  He read that perfectly, threw to the outside hand, Bateman turned and had all the space.  So that was another key conclusion.  It was interesting to see Zay less involved compared to what, you know, we had seen. It's simply harder to get the ball to Zay where he can excel when you don't have Lamar's arm. But I thought, you know, that they showed good creativity by trying to do different things with Zay.  I thought that was also an important conclusion.  So I think, overall, it was a really good halftime adjustment from Declan Doyle to try and find a way to activate Huntley, and, you have to give him credit, he succeeded.  And I simply think Huntley deserves a lot of credit.    You know, there were calls at halftime to bring Joe Flacco onto the field .  And all my mentions on Twitter, that's all people were talking about. Your mentions on Twitter.  My God, it must be, it's like entering a war zone. Another thing, Cole, that you said and when I thought you mentioned two plays, another play I want to mention is the touchdown to Devonte Walker.  Now, who made a fadeaway back pass to Devonte Walker as one of the early candidates for one of the best plays of the year?  But I loved the fact that they saw the one-on- one, had faith in a young receiver, and went after the new guy who came in for the Falcons.  The cornerback was beaten up; they had a backup cornerback who normally only plays on special teams, and they attacked him.  That's also part of the training.  We talk about it all the time.  The margin between winning and losing in the NFL is really small. Generally, I think coaches get too much credit and too much blame, but there are moments at the end of games where you can gain an advantage by doing certain things, making smart decisions, identifying that player, finding him at a key moment, and scoring that touchdown. Great throw, great catch, but also a good decision, having confidence in your player to go after that Falcons guy who's usually not on the field.  There is so much to take away from the perspective of training and the quarterback in those final offensive series. What were we talking about just a week ago tonight? How on earth are they going to improve their performance?  They are unnecessarily putting themselves behind the first down line.  Five penalties for 40 yards is a big improvement, Cole Jackson, especially knowing they used another new combination on that starting offensive line.  And , by the way, that new combination helped me run for over 200 yards against...Yes, it's an inflated number because it's a sample of only four weeks, but it was number one.  Well , after all, Atlanta had the number one run defense before the game. Loyal members of the Collective, thank you for watching this far in the video.  Jeff, Cole and I just wanted to thank you.  You have given us a lot of support over the past year since we launched this channel.  You probably already know that on Tuesday and Thursday nights, almost every week of the year, we broadcast live at 8:00 PM Eastern Time, and there's much more to come .  So, if you haven't already, subscribe so we can continue building this and bringing you Ravens content all year round. Thank you, and we'll see you again soon here at the Collective.

text: that Casey is going to practice today on a limited basis. Uh just how how nice is it for you guys to see what you saw on Sunday and then to have him out there on Wednesday? >> Well, we'll see. I mean, we're not going to rule anybody in or out today, but uh we've got a number guys dealing with some some uh some minor issues and we'll see uh today and the rest of the week. >> But how I mean, can you just how nice is I mean he was knocked out cold on the field. Uh >> Mhm. >> His eyes were rolling in the back of his head. It was a scary sight for everyone. For him to kind of have this kind of turnaround. What kind of >> No, I just from a player's health perspective, it's it's cool, you know, that it wasn't worse than it was and uh you know, so that's probably the biggest thing from a health standpoint. >> I know stats are different, but you know, facing the Ravens this week, um is there any benefit in knowing like player tendencies having worked with Lamar, having gone against, you know, a lot of those teams? Is there any any benefit, extra benefit in terms of game planning and and what not? >> I don't know about that. I mean, there's gets offset by us what we do on offense, I guess, you know, a little bit. I mean, that's who you're going to prepare for. I mean, they've got a really good coaching staff and I've been there before where we, you know, played Snoop and Snoop's a really good football player and won a bunch of games as the starter, so uh we'll prepare for the Ravens. >> Is there any emotions for you, you know, playing against them, you know, being there so long? >> I mean, it's a divisional game. I mean, that you know, and it's the next one really is what that is. I mean, did I enjoy my time there? Of course, you know, a lot of a lot of really good memories. Uh got a lot of good friends and uh people there. But, other than that, no, it's a divisional game and it's the next one. >> Coach, what is it about Snoop that you know, he's been able to work so well for so many years as, you know, kind of Lamar's understudy? >> Very confident player. You know, has a belief in himself to make plays. And he's he's really uh he's a gamer. I know it sounds really like overused, but the moment never gets too big for him. You know, he loves to play football. And um he gets in the game and he's able to make plays with his arms and his legs. And he gets rid of the ball, knows where to get the ball out when under duress. And uh you know, he works awfully hard. He's very diligent uh in preparing uh as the backup. So, when his time is called, he's able to play at a high level. >> With you and Harbaugh leaving, were you surprised how quickly they resigned >> Not really. Not not by the way we had played with him as our starter. Not after, you know, the way he played in the Bears game and then later, you know, in the Patriots second half and then uh the Packers game. I was not surprised. >> Coach, when you were in your old office there, how did you view Denzel Ward when you were getting ready to play against him? >> An elite cover guy. A guy that you know, it does a great job of staying in phase with receivers and closes on the ball well down the field. You can see that and has excellent ball skills. Be able to uh make catches at the catch point. >> How much if at all has their defense changed this year with your >> What's that? changed this year with their new coordinator? >> Oh, it it's changed dramatically in terms of I think the league has changed dramatically in terms of uh defensive coordinator's approaches um to the way the game has changed in terms of analytics and offense has taken four downs and their approach being more aggressive. But the personnel is very similar. I mean, they're they've added some pieces, but the personnel is still very similar. >> What's stood out to you about what Jack Doyle has been able to do in that offense and kind of kind of change it in this time? >> Well, you know, Jack Doyle first of all, I GA'd with his dad, so I know the family. I mean, way back at Notre Dame and GA'd for Jesse's dad who's there Rick there, so I mean, go way back with the family, but Jack Doyle is a tremendous coach. I mean, when you talk about going from New Orleans and then to Denver and has ascended quickly and really really smart. And he's doing a great job with them. I mean, been around some really good mentors, highly intelligent, doing some more under center with Lamar which is which is working. You know, the stats bear that out that they're doing a great job. >> How many of your running backs available today were not with you in training camp? You have nobody who was part of this program in training camp, I don't believe. >> Well, it's part of the next man up, right? That's that's why you keep bringing in players and getting them up to speed and and we'll see, you know, as the week goes on who we'll have available. >> When you were with the Ravens, did you say we can't throw at this guy or I don't I don't think you I >> I don't I don't think you >> Oh, I I And I this is I think Denzel is a fantastic player as there are a lot of corners out there, but I don't think there's any time you can just say we can't throw at an individual player or we can't block an individual player. There certainly there's more difficult match-ups than others, right? But you certainly have to be leery of players like that that are ball-hawking style that you know, can read routes and jump it. >> You talked about the communication in the protection game that needs to be improved. Where does that start? Is it Deshaun and Howie being on the same page? Like what needs to improve for you? >> Well, it starts with coaching. That that's where it starts. It starts with us. And that's where it always starts. It doesn't it We have to make sure that our guys are we're giving them the looks. And that we're diligent in terms of every single rep matters from the walk-through to the blitz pick-up periods. Um and we're consistent in terms of our protection and communication. That's a part of it, too. How are we coaching it? How are we scheming it? Are we giving them the right looks to start? Uh our communication, right? Up front, quarterback and center, they're the epicenter of the communication piece. And just making sure we're on the same page. And that's part of the growing pains, unfortunately, of a new system. Uh different running backs in the backfield. Young players. There's not a lot of recall there, right? Something pops up and you're like, "Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah." But that's And that's that's not an excuse cuz I'm not a big excuse guy. We certainly have to find a way to be better cuz we weren't. And some of it's uh getting the ball out. Some of it's coaching. Some of it's communication. Some of it's diligence. And uh but we know it has to be fixed. >> With Dalton Schultz being designated for return and being eligible to practice, do you anticipate him I guess being out on the practice field today? And will you monitor him throughout the week? Is there a chance he can play on Sunday? >> I think there's a chance. you know, he'll be out there today. And we're excited that uh that his window's been opened. >> You mentioned that there are more and more under center to be a league wide trend under center kind of now. >> Back a little bit. Why do you think that's a a trend across the league? >> Oh, you'd have to ask the you know, I mean the teams that that do it. I think that's everybody's comfortable with where they've been and what you know. You only coach what you know. I think obviously some of the run game, there's it's more advantageous to be under center. I think your play action game, your nakeds, I think play off of that. I think everybody would say that. So, that that's a part of it. >> advantageous for the run game to to start under center. you're at the home position, right? You don't have an offset back, right? There's no tells at times. Uh cuz then you're constantly having to move your back or you have to be in what the pistol, right? Which teams have gone to. You saw that uh with the Falcons last year, you know, with Bijan being in the in the pistol. So, I mean, all of it's good football. It's just deciding where you want to start and what you do from whether you're under center or offset or whether you're in the pistol, all of it's good football. >> Is it harder to have designed quarterback runs under center? >> It is. It's a lot more difficult. I mean, you certainly can. I mean, I um the Bears against the Was it against Carolina Panthers the first game? They ran like a little naked, but they were blocking for him. Wasn't even a naked. So, it's not very common. It's not very common to have QB driven. You're going to have more naked's. Uh you're not going to use the quarterback nearly as much. But I did see one. You made me think about that, Tony. >> Uh you obviously had your unique ways of using Zay Flowers when you were in Baltimore. Just how have you seen him get better and better as a player both in your time there and I know this year he's talked a lot about how he's getting moved around a lot more. Just how have you seen him even get better this year? >> Oh, first of all, uh from the moment he got there, I mean, you could see his skill set that was beyond a novelty. You know, you could see that his ability to route run and stay full speed, his balance and body control is elite. And uh just his personality, what he brought every single day in terms of work. Loves to practice. Got a smile on his face. And um he's just continued to get better and better. And it was hard the first year cuz we wanted to move him around. And we we moved him around, maybe not as much as they're moving him around now. but we we did move him around, but it's much harder when you're a younger player. But we certainly were trying to put Zay in position uh to catch as many balls he could and I don't care how many balls you get him, it's not enough. >> Philosophically, why is it Why is it harder to to cover um any wide receiver that lines up in the slot as opposed to if it's on the boundary? >> What's that now? >> Philosophically, why is it harder to to kind of keep a eye out or kind of guard any receiver that lines up in the slot as opposed to on the outside? >> Oh, I don't know. I guess you could argue that the distance between the throw and the player is easier. I mean, you're talking about the distance of a throw from a slot as a general rule. You're getting more and more choice routes out of those guys. You're getting more intermediate routes. Again, the distance is a part of that. I think at times your match-up gets created with nickels or safeties, that's a part of that. Um and I think you also have body types that are guys so a lot of times in the slot that create that type of separation. So, I think there's a lot more than just one thing, but I I off the top of my head, that's what hit my brain. >> Greg Roman's a big part of the Ravens last year, not so much this year. Has that been a little easier to prepare for them defensively? >> Little bit. But, you know, with what they do um under center uh their run play action and naked game, maybe from a personnel standpoint, it's a little bit different, but uh you know, with what they do and the players they have, very difficult to defend. >> Trying to get two rookies on a completely rebuilt offensive line, what what strides have you seen in the last couple of weeks out of the entire group? And I know it's complicated by some injuries and some other variables. >> of all, we didn't handle the elements very well the other day, but I'd started to see strides, you know, playing against Pittsburgh and you You Jets were a little bit more aggressive. What I've seen is we took a step back a little bit in communication, obviously in protections. But, in terms of running off the football, I've seen strides there. I've seen our confidence build with our right guard and our left tackle, the rookies. And um I think that's only going to continue to grow. And the guys in terms of playing together, I think they're just going to continue to get better and better. >> I was going to say, is it time on task as far as the communication thing is concerned? >> Some of it's that and some of it's you just going to have to make a decision. I mean, that's you have to make a decision. There's a 40-second clock. You don't you don't have all day. It's it's like taking, if you remember back, taking the ACT and the SAT. You're going to have to answer the question. You're going to run out of time. You're not If you had all day, that's different. We don't have all day. I mean, there's a clock. You have to make a decision and live with it and know where your going and know where your issues are. And uh that starts with us as coaches and making sure we are on point. And then it's up to the players once we get it in there, like, this is what we're doing and be on be on point. >> All right, two more. >> Was there any awkwardness last January working for the Ravens trying to get this job? You know, speaking of it. >> Absolutely not. Um I would say that I'm very grateful for the opportunity. you know, where basically John was let go and they allowed me to, you know, work in my office and prepare uh for the interview that I had here cuz it was initially on Zoom. So, I did that out of my office. I continued to work out of my office. I was allowed to continue to keep working there. And um again, they didn't have to do that, you know. Um so, that part of it wasn't awkward for me. I mean, it was I was trying to get another job. Like, I I don't think it was awkward for them. We'd been around it for 3 years. I mean, there's a lot of appreciation of me for the people in the building and I would think there's appreciation for the job that I did every day there. >> All right. >> You um you You talked about next man up and but when you look at the you know the number of guys that you know aren't available to practice, do you adjust anything based on that or >> We'll adjust We'll adjust today. There'll be a little bit There'll be a little more walk-through in certain periods today that we have to do. We just We just don't We won't have the numbers uh with the availability of our team. That doesn't We still have to get get full speed work in certain areas and we will do that. >> Coach, get this last one in. >> The history between these two teams obviously is well documented both here and I'm sure in Baltimore. Obviously, you were here before, but is it weird being the head coach on the other side of it knowing the history between these two? >> Not really. I mean I I don't know if that's the answer that everybody wants to hear. I mean it's ultimately I have a job to do just like I had a job to do there just like I had a job to do in '19. And the job is what can I do today to help our team get better and keep taking strides uh to play winning football. And that's that's really all I think about. I mean there's other times. I mean, you know, I mean it's a divisional game. It's a big game for us and it's the next one. That's really as much as anything is we're just trying to continue to uh develop our players and play as clean a football and you know, offensively three of the last four games we really haven't turned it over, but we ended up, you know, late in the last game and that that that gives us a chance. We got to continue down that path of not turning the ball over. Hasn't always been clean, but you know, the Pittsburgh game that stopped us, but the other two games and then yet and then, you know, Sunday gave us a chance. >> Thank you.
