But if we can all be on the same page and know the complete game plan, and not just one position, then it will go much better.  But all the guys are doing a great job making sure we all learn the full concept.  So, regardless of whether they call you up and you haven't played that position all year or all week, you'll be ready for those opportunities. Deshaun, when you have a quarterback and a receiver who have a couple of dropped passes, like Isaiah on Sunday, what do you say to that person in the game to try to help with the situation? Just encourage him.  Keep working hard, keep finding ways to get free, and I'll keep looking for you.  Those opportunities will continue to arise. Just make the next move.  We cannot think about the previous one.  So when the next opportunity comes, just make the move.  That? Under those conditions, do you think it's more difficult to throw the ball or to catch it?    I think both.  I think both.  Do you expect Baltimore to push as hard as you expected? Well, I honestly have no idea. We'll see how the game unfolds and if that's what they want to do, we'll be ready, and if not, we just have to operate and try to set up plays and find other ways to attack them. How did K'Lavon end up with a reception for four yards?  I believe he had a total of four directed passes .  Don't know.  Was he supposed to be more of a blocker, or what happened to K'Lavon in that game? Again, it's just the flow of the game and how the plays are being called, honestly. Deshaun, this offensive line has been rebuilt from the ground up and you guys have had some injuries too.  How difficult has it been to build that cohesion and the chemistry you need between that unit and you? Well, again, it's just more repetition, more opportunities we have, communication throughout the week, watching videos together, seeing what we're saying, basically communicating what I'm seeing and what they're seeing, and just trying to be on the same page as much as possible.  So, again, we have five new guys, two of them are rookies, and three who come from , you know, different backgrounds.  You know, we just integrate everyone and try to communicate and possible. How much do you, as a quarterback, need the running game to work? Well, I mean, it's definitely useful, you know, in general, not just for the quarterback position, but for the whole team.  You know, being able to run with the ball is definitely one of the hardest things you have to do in this league;  But , when you can do it, it definitely opens up many other possibilities. How do you stay on course as the leader of this offense, with an opportunity like this and, you know, with a record of four and one, after having let slip a game that they certainly feel they should have won? How do you keep the ship afloat and these young guys focused, knowing that everything is at stake and that on Sunday they'll be fighting for first place? Yes, it's a long season.  It's an opportunity that's right in front of us.  We can't dwell on what happened on Sunday.  You know, we watched the recording on Monday, we have the 24-hour rule, we had Tuesday off and today we're back to focus on the next opponent. So the opportunity is right there in front of us, and we have to work hard during the week to be prepared and have the chance to take advantage of it on Sunday. What are some of the keys to having a successful screen game, and do you feel you're not where you want to be in that area yet? Screen game? Screen game.    I mean , it's really just that, for the guys to know their marks, to know who they're going to block, and, you know, just be able to execute the timing properly.  All those things have to be in sync so that, you know, whoever receives the ball can catch it and move forward. It seems that his chemistry with the offense grows stronger every week.  Could you talk about your relationship and how it continues to grow between you? Yes, I mean, he has been able to approach me from a young age and communicate what he sees, and I think the most important thing is that he can grasp the information I give him and also the information given to him by the coaching staff. So, being someone who learns quickly , understands, and has the cunning to make plays, he has been able to take advantage of them when the opportunity arises.  So , you know, all of that combined has given him more opportunities and he's making the most of them.  Therefore, our relationship continues to grow, we continue to build that bond, and we hope to continue creating more plays.  Do you think two more? Uh... No, I don't know, I mean, I'm... I was at the opposite end, so I couldn't really see well.  I mean , I saw the pictures and stuff like that. I know Maker was just making a play and trying to make a play, but yeah, I guess that's just how football is.  You know, I'm just glad Casey is healthy and doing much better, no doubt. DeShawn, you're obviously familiar with Kyle Hamilton's game from the past.  Uh, matches against him.  They added Starks to the mix this year with their first pick.  How difficult are those guys in the back in terms of what you see, how they move, and the versatility they offer? Yes, they are key players.  You know, those guys are, especially Hamilton , an All-Pro player.  Starks, I believe in his second year, is on his way to becoming an All-Pro.  You know, those guys are playing at a very high level for that defense, and they have other good players on that defense as well.  So , this is a great challenge for us to be able to go out there and test who we are.  And well, you know, we just have to be on the same page and see what they're doing, and make sure that, you know, we have those players under control on every play. And finally, we're left with this one. Although you didn't play against them, you were present at the meetings when they played against the Ravens last year.  Do you see any difference in their defense after this coaching change? Uh, the truth is I don't even remember last year, so I couldn't tell you.  I only remember the players I played against, so there are a lot of familiar faces, but hey , you know, they're doing a great job on defense, no doubt.    I Thank you.

title: Klint Kubiak and Kirk Cousins Presser - 10.14.26
text: Morning. Uh, Tonka won't practice today. I hope to get Jaylen back tomorrow. I'll take any of your guys questions. >> Clint, going back yesterday and looking at the film from last year with Seattle, people stacking the box against you is not something you're not used to or even using cover zero, but I noticed there was a lot of slants and rubs. Would you like to see that implemented more in that situation with your Raiders, sir? >> Uh, talking about the pass game or the run game? >> The passing game, sir. when when that box is stacked using some slants and rubs and >> Absolutely. Yeah. Just uh you know trying to attack what the defense gives you and there's um you know when when you're getting man coverage that's always an option. Yes. >> You talked about potentially making some changes up front or switching it up. just promoting I'm sorry to cut you off but yes just promoting competition and uh >> you know we there's whether it's corner this week or guys on the offensive line this week there's always competition and you know I think that that gets the player the players to play their best you know but just telling someone that he's going to go this week u you know I don't think that's fair to the Raiders or to the players so really want to promote competition especially offensive line and a corner this week >> you brought up the corner competition between Darien and and Zeke, but also how's Grammad developing and can he factor in that competition as well? >> Yeah, he certainly can. You know, uh, he certainly can. We're we're counting on him. We know we drafted him for a reason. Um, you know, more specifically, I see DP and Zeke, you know, fighting for who's going to start the game and we know that everybody's going to play. >> How do you see from Ashton this week during practice? And also with that being said, Mike Washington Jr. as well, just to see if he gets some more reps. Yeah, you know, I think Ashton is is really starting to feel a lot better physically. So, excited about giving him even more reps in practice and um you know, more full speed reps and with Mike and with Dylan, all those guys have to factor in for us. >> There was a report this morning that there was internal conversations about giving Ashton a week off. I guess is that true? And is is has that been a discussion recently? >> Uh he's playing. When you face someone like Josh Allen with the stress he puts on his secondary, not only for his passing, but just his running ability, how how difficult is that? >> Yeah, very difficult. You know, he's an elite athlete, elite thrower. Um, great instincts to know when to run and uh, you know, definitely between between Cook and and the quarterback, you know, those are those are two guys that can really hurt you with their legs. >> What's the biggest opportunities against Buffalo to take control of this game offensively and control tempo? Yeah. Well, you know, you got to get first down to stay on the field. So, you know, going three and out. Putting the ball back is not the way to go. So, you got to sustain drives. That's a big part of sustaining drives is being, you know, not being onedimensional. So, that's a part of our team that we got to improve. >> Do you feel like uh creating turnovers through the first three weeks somewhat hid some of the weaknesses that your defense has had? Uh, you know, uh, I think that you do what you got to do to win the game and you know, the your weaknesses come out and you know what the numbers say that say that they are and we're just trying to go win the game, you know, so we're trying to improve all of our weaknesses. That's offensive, defense, special teams, and uh, you know, you know, the other side of the ball is going to they're going to come after what you're good at. They're going to harp on, hey, this team, you know, they've taken the ball away, so they're going to protect it better. So, we got to um continue to take the ball away and just continue to improve as a team. >> I just when you look when you look back at this film, not just from the Patriots game over recent weeks, where do you feel like you guys can improve on in terms of run blocking? >> Uh yeah, many areas. And you know, it's it's it's coaching. It's it's playing. And you know, at the end of the day, you we kind of go back to the basics and make sure you're focused on the fundamentals and not trying to get too cute with your schemes and, you know, just giving guys a good plan they can go execute fast. >> I know that you didn't win on Sunday and for you, it's all about the team, but Adam Butler is playing at a very good level right now. Could you discuss his performance, please? >> Yeah, great question. I think I think AB just from the start has been such a leader here. uh just the way that he works, the type of professional that he is, and um you know, I think your guy's true character sticks out. You know, when you're when you're playing at the end of a game, you're down multiple scores and um look no further than his character, you know, showing up, making plays. >> How do you foster that competition you talked about during a week when you're trying to prepare for a game and there's only so much opportunity to do it? >> Yeah. Uh well, you know, jobs on the line that that fosters it. There is only so many arrests, but it's the NFL and you know, that's why you have training camp. That's why you have the offseason and we got we got plenty of reps under our belt. So, um yeah, there's not there's not a ton during the week, but you know, there's enough there's enough to get ready to play a football game. >> Obviously, having Brad Bowers is a luxury on this team, but without everything he can do, how much emphasis do you put on the other receivers to make sure that they're also equally doing their part to kind of open up more space for him to do what he does. >> Yeah, you know that everyone we need everybody to move the ball. We need everybody. So, um Brock's doing a good job. I think his teammates are doing a good job and they just they're more deserving of opportunities. So that's that's on myself and the coaching staff of getting them in position. >> I you are a film guy. You love to show your team film. And so I'm curious in a loss like that one. Is it much better to teach when you're able to show guys on film rather than you just talking? Is that is that help you as a teacher? >> Yeah, that's the that's the best tool. You know, uh the guys are visual. You know, you can only tell them so much if you show them. Uh, it definitely helps get your point across. You know, that's definitely something that I like to do. A lot of coaches on our staff like to do, but um, you know, you got to make the correction somehow some way. So, whatever hits the players brain the fastest, you got to use that technique. >> How would you assess your the interior of your offensive line play specifically the guard play? >> Yeah, I I it's a it's a group effort. So, as a group, you know, we've uh overall to the to date we've protected well and we got to run better. How do you feel um you guys can get a better pass rush when opposing teams are are chipping backs? >> Yeah, we're uh you know, we've definitely been in discussion about how to be better there and you know, without getting into the details, there's you know, there's things that we are working on. Yes. >> What's that ramp up period looking like for Dante this week? What are your expectations? What do you want to see from him? >> Yeah, he's just got to got to prove to us he's ready to go play in the NFL game. You know, conditioning's there that uh you know, he's you know, he's he didn't have a whole lot of training camp guys. He's he's coming back from a lot of time off, but he's worked really hard and he's put himself in a position last week to prove, you know, prove to us this week and maybe next week that he's ready to go. >> You still gone? >> I am not. >> Sorry. I was I was curious Dante, what is like the like what are the certain benchmarks you're looking for as during practice for him to kind of like overcome so he's ready or you know he's ready to go? >> Yeah, just with any player coming back from an injury that's been out for a long time. Number one is conditioning and uh number two is you know being assignment sound and number three is making plays. >> Going back to knowing you like to talk about team I have a specific player question but about DJ Glaze when you watched the film on Sunday I thought he of all your offensive line in my opinion it looked like he had his best day. Your opinion is more valuable. Can you just assess how he's playing right now? Please Clint >> I can. Uh you know DJ's I think one of our most consistent guys. You know he never misses practice. uh he's always getting better and uh the game's really important to him. So I think he's becoming, you know, he's becoming a quiet leader that needs to f can even find his voice more, you know, because his teammates respect him as as does coaching staff. >> What was your that you said you wanted to um uh fix and look at this week, especially when there are a lot of things as a coaching staff, how do you determine what your main focus is going to be as you progress through the week? >> Yes, you got to keep it bite-sized. you know, you got to give them, you know, if you're going to try to accomplish something, then it's you got to be very intentional about those things. And if your list is trying to do 10 things, it's probably not going to be very good at them. So, just trying to, you know, give them intentional coaching points that we can accomplish each day. >> You abandoned the run game too early this past weekend. How do you assess or measure that in game when it's not working versus keep harping at home? >> Yeah, that's that's part of the game. game within the game, you know, and you rely on your coaching staff and uh as you're as you're talking on the headset together and going through strategy, you know, for each series and um that's there's an art to it and it's not perfect. >> Coach, going back to what you want to emphasize, the bite sizees, I guess, what are I guess the biggest bites you're going to take first this week? >> Yeah. >> Um you know, guys, we there's no question that we have to run the football and stop the run better. What were your thoughts on the way that Dylan Lobby stepped up in uh last week's game and his use overall in offense? >> Yes. Uh not surprised. He's he's a very consistent player for us on special teams and that carries over into offensive football and he's earned earned his opportunities. >> What does Darren Johnson meant for this defense? >> Uh professional. He's he's a pro. He's a leader. >> There was some uh pretty high-profile game management, clock management situations around the league this week. Uh, how much does that help as a coaching staff to to have those things on tape and be able to teach from them and for players to be reminded like they have to have responsibility too of what's going on? >> Yes. You know, I we have uh you know, between uh Rohead and Joe D and Mike McCoy, they do such a great job of putting together teach tapes for our guys each week. Um, and we use we use the good and the bad every week from around the league to make sure that, you know, we're on top of our stuff. >> There's been some questions about Ashton getting back to his college stance. Is that something you've considered or what went into the process of changing that? >> Uh, you know, those are those are things that are between Ash and myself and his coaches and you know, bottom line is we just got to find more production and starts with the coaching staff and putting our players in best position to be successful. >> All right, thanks coach. >> Appreciate it. >> Thanks Morning guys. Um, yeah, just another good football team we've got this week. Uh, you know, it' be great to be back home. Uh, have a couple home games now and, uh, looking forward to the challenge. So, take any questions you have. >> Kurt, going back even to Holland Christian High School, you have always been gifted at the pre-nap read and I'm just curious when teams are stacking the box or throwing in some cover zero. How much even more critical is the pre-nap lead for an NFL quarterback at nowadays? >> Yeah, no, pre-nap's very important. I would say post snap, you know, really probably becomes more important. um uh you know, and then there's teams who want to hide their zeros. There's teams that are going to show it and then there's teams that are going to show it and then bail out of it and they're not going to play zero. So, you kind of get uh a variety of looks and um uh you do the best you can pre- snap and then you also know that regardless of what decisions you make pre- snap or what you're going with, then you got to react post snap and make good good decisions at that point. after the loss. Sorry. What have you seen about uh accountability in this locker room and how guys are responding? >> Yeah, there's just back to work. Um it's a great group. It's the same guys when I stand up here and talk in training camp or after a win about how I love the group. It's it's the same um opinion after a tough loss, you know, where you say, "Hey, this is a great group. guys uh they point the thumb not the not pointing the finger and uh just want to get better, want to learn and um and get better together and so um that's what it's about and I think it's good response but you know we got to got to show it on Sunday. >> Kurt just diving into the film from from New England I was just curious just what why do you think the Pacers are so effective in terms of creating pressure and getting getting it home? >> Well they were you know at most of the time it was they were bringing more than we were going to block. So, so not just sheer math-wise, they're going to they're going to get pressure. It's just, you know, avoiding the sack. And then the most important is, you know, getting the completion, you know. So, that was where we uh weren't able to connect. That was the miss. Um, you know, as far as they're bringing seven, we have six to block or they're bringing six, we have five to block. You know, the ball's got to go. Um, that the challenge or the miss was just not being able to, you know, throw completions, make connections. Uh, and that's where you're going back and saying, you know, I got to be better there. Clint was talking about when there's a lot of things to work on, just making it kind of bite-sized so that it can you can take this one, take this one, take this one. Throughout your career, have you seen that's the best way for you instead of saying, "Hey, we got to fix all these things of like, hey, let's just do one step at a time." >> Yeah. No, I think uh the more you can zoom focus, the more you can um make it about one technique or one fundamental that just has to be improved and then kind of allow the bigger picture to fix itself as a result of that one technique. I mean, that's the ideal way to approach it. Um, but that that analysis is such a big part of of getting better is being able to look at it and say, "Okay, let's boil this down." Um, you know, it wasn't 17 plays that all had 17 different reasons why we weren't good enough on those plays. Let's try to think what was a common theme. What was a consistent, you know, thing that we struggled with or that we can get better in. And if if we can do that, you know, that's how you can I think can get better is just having that deliberate analysis that helps you then be more productive at practice. >> I just asked Clint about but DJ Glaze is is playing well right now. Would you specifically talk about him, please? >> Yeah. Yeah. No, he's um uh done a great job I think back, you know, a couple weeks to 50 plus pass attempts and the way he, you know, was able to handle that. Um but no, he's done a great job run game, pass game, he's he's handled well. so quiet, you know, you don't really u uh notice him out there, which I always said about Christian Darasaw is a great trait when you don't really know that your old linemen are there. They're usually doing something right, not something wrong. So, um he's been great and uh we'll keep asking a lot of them up ahead. >> What do you like most about having a fullback? >> That's a great question. I I've always liked this system carrying a fullback going back to my rookie year in college. We used a fullback quite a bit. fullbacks and tight ends, I think, tend to be that Swiss Army knife player where, you know, if if you have one who's who's as versatile as you want him to be at the position, you know, he should be able to run a seam route. He should be able to, you know, set the edge and and block the edge. Um, he should be able to, you know, handle protection. So, this the ability to wear a lot of hats gives you a lot of flexibility. And um you know, it's kind of one of those theories in football where you say, you know, are you better off just being in the same personnel all game so you're not tipping anything to the defense and allowing your players to wear a bunch of hats or are you better off, you know, switching personnels all the time to kind of keep defenses guessing. And um you hear different philosophies. That's one of those fun things you kind of talk about in the offseason. But um remember my college coach made the point that one of his best years he ever had as a coach was uh they went 10 and two when he was at Kansas and it was they just went in 21 the whole game had a fullback on the field and never really changed it and asked the fullback to to wear a lot of hats and so um you know that's something Connor Hayward can do here and I think it makes a big difference. >> How how important is sticking to the run game to set up the passing game and also the play action game which you guys have done so well through the first month. Yeah, I think it's an an age-old debate of um you know, how much what is sticking to the run game, what is sticking to it too much, what is sticking to it not enough. You know, I think that's where you just have to kind of play the game from what the game calls for. But, um certainly helps when you have a lead, when you're, you know, playing well and you put yourself in a position to then be able to run the football more. Um been in a lot of games where you're down and you have to abandon the run game, not by not by your own choice, but just you're forced to. Um, but no, I think the more at bats you get, the better. And, um, uh, you know, it certainly sets up, like you said, to play action in other parts of your offense, the more you're willing to commit to it and and, uh, and make the defense believe it. >> Football Football is one of those few sports where you you practice and prepare more than you actually play. >> And I'm I'm just wondering, >> sometimes I wish it was like baseball. You just go play, you know, just just go play. >> Curious about do you do you appreciate um this part of it, the the Saturday through Saturday uh part of it? Yeah. No, I I think the unseen part of the NFL that is the NFL for us players is Monday through Saturday. Um, you know, and even myself, you know, I when I watch other people, I see Sunday and then I see Sunday. I don't see the in between. And it's the in between that really tests you mentally, tests you emotionally, tests you physically. Um, and I had no concept for it until I got in the NFL, just how much it takes to be ready for a Sunday kickoff, to play at the level you're going to need to play at. um what it takes on a Wednesday, on a Thursday, on a Friday. So, um big part of our sport. I think it would even surprise hockey and basketball and baseball if those guys were to go through our routine for a week. I think they'd say, "I had no idea um what you have to do just between games." And I think we would enjoy kind of the opportunity to just do a quick shoot around and then go play again. So, um that's the nature of our sport and uh uh you got to be great on Wednesday and Thursday and Friday to expect to be great on Sunday. After a loss like Sunday, Kirk, can there be almost paralysis by analysis? Can there be too much thinking sometimes and just a bad day? >> Certainly could be. Um um you know, I think it's that's another balance you're trying to find of um to come back in and say it's not that important. We'll move on. It's one game. That to me sounds like a losers mentality. To still be talking about it four weeks later might also be a losers mentality. So there's a middle ground there that you've got to find every week. And um that's what players and coaches have to find. But uh if I had to error on one side, it would probably be being hard on ourselves, fixing things, feeling like they've been resolved. And I think that allows you then to play with confidence moving forward. >> Throughout throughout your career, um did did you ever do like unique things to kind of help like young players get up to speed with the playbook or understand their opponents? I know Aaron Rogers kind of like gives pop quizzes to his guys. for you. What was kind of >> do you do anything on that end or something else? >> You know, I think a little bit too is the world you live in. I think in Aeron's world, it's he wants to at times call the game at the line of scrimmage, which is going to be where he's kind of becoming the offensive coordinator and he's going to give a quick hand signal here or there. And you've heard people like Devonte Adams joke about how quick and subtle that hand signal is going to be. And so Aaron knows if I don't have these pop quizzes, if I don't gather the guys at the house to go over these hand signals, you know, we're not going to be able to do that. If that's not really the world you live in, um, then it's not as much of a point of emphasis. But, uh, there's no doubt that, you know, at the end of the week, I try to compile some of the new curveballs, some of the new things. Maybe we didn't cover it as much as I thought, uh, we might need, and I'll just take a couple minutes, you know, and on Saturday night and just say, "Hey guys, like here's some things as I went back through the game plan that just to re-emphasize, to retouch on." Um, so that I know, you know, in the heat of battle that I can I can say, "Okay, we're on the same page." And um that always gives me peace of mind even if I'm not getting you know even if they already knew it. It's sometimes just I say to them hey me saying it to you helps me now play with confidence and assuredness because I know that the message got to you >> Eric after watching the film it's easier to see what adjustments you could have made in game in terms of getting the offense going through the last two games. What have you noticed is a common theme and ways that you could adjust mid game that haven't really been executed? >> Basically you're asking how can we play better on offense the last two weeks. Uh, you know, I think I think it is you could compartmentalize it and say, well, at the end of the game against the Chiefs, you know, would have loved to have handled that final snap differently. Um, uh, you know, I think we moved the ball well against the Chiefs. Uh, I think it was a play here, a play there, maybe a third down here, third down there. I als I'd say the same about the Patriots. A couple of third downs you want back. Um, but, uh, very different defenses and so also hard to say, oh, you know, here's a common theme. I think there's a little bit of, you know, what Chiefs were doing and what the Patriots were doing. We're kind of living in two different worlds and um um probably then require different answers as to how to be better. >> Uh Ashton's working through some health things like what's it like to see him battling and >> Yeah. No, he's been he's he's been tough. Um um you know, and and he's done a great job and positive attitude and and so I think that's that all you know it helps everybody at practice. you know, when you see someone one of your star players, you know, practicing hard, um, you know, having a positive attitude, I think it brings everybody else up, too. So, he's doing a great job and, um, he'll keep doing it. >> You, uh, you don't come off as the influencer type, but you, uh, >> like social media influencer. >> You've you become the king of going viral a little bit. What is that like it happened again this week where like >> Did it really you got on the plane? Yeah. The pregame your pregame speech was like >> Oh, it was again. >> Yeah. So, >> I didn't even see that. >> Okay. I guess so. >> Yeah. So, you're I'm getting news. Okay. >> What What is What are those experiences like that you've had in the past over it's like after a game you playing for three hours and you find out like, "Oh, everybody's talking about what I did." >> Yeah. I didn't I didn't know that. I think you are my social media here updating me. But, um maybe it's the fact that you what you started with and you say you're not an influencer and it's like that's probably why is that if people don't expect it from me, maybe it is a bit of a curveball. But, I would say the people who don't expect it from me probably don't know me, you know? And I think you've heard some teammates here even say it like, "Oh, I didn't I didn't know Kirk was the way he is from a distance and then he joined our team and was around us and I started to say, "Oh, okay. That's what he's like." That's I think sometimes the perception reality can be different and when when people start to see reality instead of perception, maybe sometimes they go, "Oh, that's that's kind of entertaining." So, I don't know. >> Take his change. >> You know what? we need to win and then we can talk all we want about uh about celebrating in chains and flights home and uh but you can't do it if you don't win. So um you know let's go win some games and see what see what happens. >> Being a vet >> um Clint talked about uh Mike Washington needing some more opportunities. What what can he provide for the offense? >> Yeah. No, Mike's has a lot of juice and I think he's shown that going back to practices. Uh you guys have seen it and so um uh you know you always get back the end of a game. I even do it myself and I I'm not necessarily calling the plays or kind of scheming it up, but I think, you know, did we get this guy enough touches? Is this guy getting the ball enough? How many targets? So, and I'm even thinking of myself of, you know, am I am I spreading the football around? Not that I decide that in the moment, but just trying to be aware of making sure that who's who's not getting enough touches and and can I help with that? So, um you know, Mike's one of those guys that I think good things happen when the football's in his hand and you want those kind of guys on your team and you want them uh impacting the game. So, um, you know, hopefully you can do that up ahead. >> Being a vet, you've been in tough games like last week. What's the biggest things you learned in those moments throughout your career that can allow this to snowball? >> Yeah, I mean, I'll I'll be a broken record saying it, but tough times don't last, tough people do. Um, stay the course, get back to work. Um, you can't have the poor me and you can't brush it off as no big deal. I think it's somewhere in the middle. You have to find that balance of how you come back to work with, um, you know, it hurts. it matters to you, but at the same time, new week, you know, I remember when I sat with Philip Rivers a few years ago in the offseason, asked him questions. One of the things that stuck with me among many was he said, "Kirk, every Wednesday, you got to come in, new week, you know, positive attitude, new week, flush whatever happened, come into the cafeteria with a smile on your face, excited, ready to go." And uh that's always stuck with me. >> There were some moments around the league this week with some clock management things, not not asking you to go after, but how much does that help to just have those things where you say, "Hey, look, talk to your teammates, talk to your coaches. How do we handle these kinds? >> We we we call it the fourth phase. You know, you got three phases in football. The fourth phase is situational game management and you got to be a situational master and we talk about it in OTAAS. We talk about it through training camp. Uh we have presentations every week about what's going on around the league. Uh you know, Road does a great job with our situational management, but there is so much every walkthrough we try to simulate a situation and and walk and talk through it and and play through it. And um it's difficult. You know, I wish I had been better at the end of the Chiefs game. So sometimes the bullets are flying, it's going fast, and you got a lot to process. But, um, the better you can handle those situations, they tend to be the the inches that that make the difference.

title: Colts bring back LB Germaine Pratt, begin practice for Titans
text: There have been weeks where you guys have run the ball really really well, other weeks where you guys were very effective moving the ball in the passing game, but not as effective in the red zone. What does it take to find more balance within the offense? >> Uh yeah, I mean I think it just comes down to to executing. Um certain games you're going to play out differently and and take advantage of the opportunities we have to make plays. Uh whether that's run game or pass game, the objective is to score points and and we got to do that. >> You mentioned that Josh has been seeing extra attention on third down. How many weeks has has that kind of been going on now? >> Um yeah, I don't know. Every week's different. Every team game plans a little bit differently, so um you know, we'll we'll see what this week looks like, but um yeah, you know, at least several weeks I think that you've seen teams keying on him on third down. >> How do you guys prepare things up for Jonathan in the in the box? Is it just about executing in the vertical game? >> Uh yeah, like I said, every team's going to play a little bit differently. Um so I think it's about executing when we when we have the looks. Uh when we have good looks to run it, you know, we'll run it and we we have good looks to throw it, we'll throw it and we got to do that well. >> Upon looking at the tape, what are some things in the red zone that you feel you guys didn't do to to complete drives? >> Um well, I mean I think there was two kind of two two series where we didn't score, right? One of them we were in there tight and and um you know, couldn't couldn't get in there. Um ran it a few times, the other one we were a little further out and threw it a few times, we couldn't get in. So, you know, I think it's just about about executing and and whether we're running it, whether we're throwing it, whether we're tight, whether we're um you know, a little further away, we got to find a way to score. So, um that's the that's the goal at the end of the day. >> Daniel, how does it change things with going back to the question about Daniel when you're able to get some uh some traction on first down, you know, and and get a manageable second and third down? Just How does that change things when you're able to to get into that? >> Yeah, I think it makes a big difference. I think um you know, I thought you know, I don't know what exactly the numbers look like last week, but I thought we did a pretty good job on first down in some situations and keeping the chains moving, getting first downs on some first downs. So, continue to try to try to do that. But, yeah, I think playing in a advantageous situation to the offense and in second and short or third and short, it's certainly a good thing for us. >> Facing a Titans team that's struggled so far this season, what's your mentality heading into this week on Sunday? >> Yeah, huge game. It's a divisional game at home. We know how important that is. You know, we we know we've got to got to be ready to go and got to play a good game on Sunday. So, we'll go through the the week preparing like we always do and and got to shore up some of the things that we haven't done as well and be ready to go on Sunday. >> You see their record, 0 and 5. How do you not get caught up in that and just we can't take them lightly. You got to got to stay focused. >> Yeah, I think this is the NFL. All these games are big. These these games are important. You know, like like I said, it's a divisional game at home and and you know, we we got to be ready to go. >> So, you wearing the gloves last Sunday? Will you practice with it? Is that something you'll continue to do again on game day? >> Yeah, I'm not sure. That was something just with the the weather forecast. It was something I was planning on doing and just kind of stuck with it. So, you know, I'm I'm not sure about that. I'll see how it goes. I don't think it makes a big difference either way. >> In your experience against the Robert Saleh defense, what kind of I guess unique challenges >> Um, yeah, I think you know, obviously a good system, system that's been successful in the NFL for a long time now and you see a lot of other teams have, you know, run a similar style, similar philosophy. So, it's a good system. They're they're sound. They're they're in the right spots. You know, they they know what you know, know what they're supposed to do and they they execute that. So, Um, I think, you know, for us it's about being disciplined, making sure we uh are in the right spots on offense, spreading the field out, um finding the completions. >> Tyler's seen a heavier workload the last few weeks. How much reliability does he bring to this offense? >> A lot. Yeah, I think Tyler's uh been big for us, for sure. Had a Had a great game on Sunday and and we'll continue to try to get him the ball uh when we can. >> You may be getting him the ball a lot. How important is it to get the numbers of the other receivers up though? >> Yeah, we're trying to get everybody the ball. Uh trying to trying to help everybody make plays and um that's the goal. >> You're going back to the same stadium and still trying to stay like I guess in NFL mode. >> I mean, it's it's it's great, you know, you just like, you know, I never experienced this like being able to being a free agent for so long, you know, but obviously going back to college, being around them young guys, seeing how much joy they brought me, just being around um my old coach, coach, my old head coach, just being around him, uplift me, helping me with my mental. Um it was it was great. >> How surprised you'd be back here? >> Um I mean, opportunity come, you you take advantage of it. >> Did you have other teams that reached out and I guess what made the Colts the right fit? >> Um I think like I I had a workout with Dallas and then 2 weeks later the Colts called, so it was like opportunity come. >> You're on the practice squad right now, but you have a feeling it'll be a matter of time before you're back in there. What's the plan? >> Um I don't know the plan, you know, I'll be ready when my opportunity come, you know, obviously I'm on practice squad, I help help guys and be the best teammate I can be. That's That's my job and that's my goal, and I elevate the room and just help them be successful. >> How do you think you can help the defense? >> Um just I think last year I came in I was stable, helped to stable position, but now helping defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know, you know, so it helped me stable, accelerate down, make tackles, whatever case may be, or get some turnovers. >> What is the the um mental side of you going to free agency the team doesn't resign you obviously goes in a little bit of a different direction and then five weeks into the season comes calling back like how how what have you made of that is there anything to that? >> I mean this is a part of business I never experienced like I said you know it's a always a blessing to play in the national football league it don't matter what what may don't go your way but you know you always have faith you believe in God and take day by day you know I have a great support system too around me so they just help me keep on working and opportunity may come. >> Did you want to resign here in the spring? I wanted to I just wanted an opportunity to play football again. >> From your understanding is the plan to still play at Will linebacker? >> Uh I mean that's what I played so yeah. >> This linebacker room looks quite a bit different than the last time that you were here what asset can you be what can you bring especially given how much you know about this defense in particular? >> Um just the leadership you know elevate the room just helping the guys process it faster understanding they help with the defense understanding the scheme and helping them grow you know each and every week. >> Given your relationship with Lou and your connection to the team how much had you been following this defense over the early part of the season? >> Uh I've been following somewhat a little bit not not too much. >> Sounds like you I assume you know Akeem pretty well based off of your Cincinnati days. >> Yeah um obviously um me and Akeem know each other since we was young he live in Thomasville I live in High Point so he like 15 minutes away from me and then him playing playing with him five years in Cincinnati was huge. >> So you knew him before? >> Yeah I knew him before yeah he's 15 minutes down the road from me. what's I mean you've been a what would you call it like a an unbiased observer when you've watched the Colts through the first five weeks this defense what what do you feel like is needed to get back to the football that you guys want to be playing? >> Um just everybody just running to the ball, you know, their hair on fire, uh, physical on defense, they attack the ball, get some turnovers, you know, it's huge, you know. You get turnovers, you get more opportunity for things on to make plays or JT getting the ball in his hand or Warren getting the ball, you know, and or Downs being able to score one touchdowns, you know, just just getting the ball away, just being this is this being a dominant defense. >> Cam, the individuals within this defense have spoken so much about holding one another accountable. What is the standard that you are holding guys to as you guys prepare for a critical week with a divisional game ahead of you? >> Um, just leaving no boxes unchecked. I think, um, this week, especially with, um, our up and down performances that we've had, we just want to lock in on every single detail and make sure, one, that effort, um, all the controllable things are are done to like to 100%, um, the communication, knowing our assignments, those things that are controllable, making sure those are taken care of cuz that should never be a question on game day. Then everything else after the after the ball snaps, then that'll take care of itself. So, I think, um, just the collective understanding that we all have to be in the right spots and, you know, every single person doing their one of 11 is going to make really us have consistent performances and do it do it at a better job. So, yeah. >> You mentioned those up and down performances, the lack of consistency. >> Mhm. >> What's attributed to that? >> Um, it's it's football, so it's going to be a little bit of everything, different things every single week. Um, fixing mistakes that we've made and trying not to repeat them, but also, um, a phrase that coach says, "Nailing the knowns." The things that we should know, the like I said, communication before the snap, all that should be the things that we should be 100% on because it's it's up to us. That that comes down to preparation. So, I think, um, just the up and down weeks come down to execution on our job as players and we have to take accountability, like you mentioned already, that we have to be accountable to the person next to us because if I don't do my job, now it's going to make the person next to me his job a lot harder. So for, you know, just moving forward, everybody is really, especially for me as a safety and as a communicator back there, I want to do above and beyond my job extremely well so the guys around me can feel confident to do their job because if one person doesn't do their job, now another guy has to, you know, compensate for that then now they don't do their job to 100%. So I think it's just that collective understanding and that's the focus for this week. >> What does that accountability and effort look like in practice that you need to prepare yourself to play that way on Sunday? >> Yeah, I think just practicing to exhaustion. I think just taking it that next step and I think we've had really good practices. I've been happy with our preparation every single week so when we don't play well on Sundays for me it's like, okay, we need to figure out what more can we do because we wouldn't as leaders on the team, we wouldn't let us go Wednesday, Thursday, Friday not having good practices and be okay with it. With that being said, we've been practicing really well but it needs to show up in the game. So I think it not showing up in the game just tells us as leaders, okay, we need to do a little more. But everybody look at themself in the mirror. Like for me, I'm going to run and touch the ball carrier every single time, every single play, every snap of practice. I'm going to I don't care how far they are. Like that's my my message to myself. I need to practice with that type of effort and it'll be contagious and I think that that's just the culture we need to create in ourselves around the player to player and we have it already but just doing it above and beyond. I think we're at this point we need to be extra about everything. The extra work and just cuz we know we have a lot of football ahead of us. We want a lot we want good football ahead of us. We don't want to just settle for, you know, a good 2 weeks then go down a week. We want to be getting better throughout the year and that's where for me personally, I'm going to be extremely extra the next you know, practices throughout the rest of the season and I'm going to test my body and see how how hard I can go in practice and see and I know it'll pay off in the game. >> You got a winless team coming in here, but how important is it to not overlook that fact and take the right approach to this situation? >> Yeah, every every NFL team is capable of beating beating you. So, if you don't come in prepared, if you don't have a good practice, a good walk-through, good meetings, then at the end of the day, you're going to you're setting yourself up to get beat. So, I think we have to focus as if we're as the Super Bowl, and that's really the focus every single week that no matter who we play, and and it's a division game. So, no matter who you're playing, those are always tight games, no matter the record, no matter what what they've done. They played good teams, also, so they've been tested and gone gone against really good players. So, they'll be ready, and we got to be ready for them. >> How important you mentioned takeaways as something that needs to improve. What needs to [clears throat] change defensively to be able to take the ball away more now? >> I think just more more guys to the ball. I think population, pursuit. There's a phrase, the four P's, if I can remember them off the top of my head. Population, pursuit, probably punching at the ball. It's it's the high school phrase that we had, but there's a lot of things, but I think population or being around the ball brings the most, you know, best chances to get a turnover, whether it's tip balls, whether it's punch out, and just opportunities. And I think just us focusing on that, and like that comes with effort, that comes from everybody being, you know, in zone. We're all breaking on the balls and seeing the quarterback and seeing where the ball is going to be. If we're in man, we're covering our guy, and the ball will come to the quarterback's throwing to your guy. So, I think just knowing where our opportunities are and being extremely like extremely nasty to try and get to the football. I think we just have to bring that intensity and be a lot more intense trying to get the ball out. And obviously, it's a focus now because we're behind, but we know that we know that we'll get back on track with that. >> it is kind of hard to picture you nasty. >> I'll [laughter] figure it out. I had a lot of a lot of turnovers last year, and I'm disappointed in my performance this year cuz I started really fast last year. I was able to get the ball a lot. So, I feel like I've, you know, I pride myself on being a ball hawk. So, I'm going to I'm going to find a way to to get that ball. So, I'll be you'll see the intensity and just the the grit increase for me, for sure. >> Cuz you're always so jovial. Yeah. >> Yeah. I'll be happy, but I'll be Yeah, I'll be trying to rip somebody's head off or rip the ball out of their hand with a smile on my face still. So, just cuz I enjoy doing it. >> Had an opportunity to ask Daniel about how much reliability you bring to the offense when it's whatever is tasked upon you, running the ball, catching the ball, whatever it might be. How much pride do you take just in that reliability and whatever factor it might be week to week? >> Yeah, I think that um that's something I enjoy about tight end position, right? You do a lot of different stuff and and get to, you know, do different stuff in the offense. So, I think that's kind of what our room takes pride in, being reliable and stuff like that. >> I know week to week the game plans are different, but certain weeks you guys have been so effective running the ball with Jonathan. Other weeks you've moved the ball really well, but stalled out in the red zone. What does it take to find more balance, more consistency within your offense? >> Um I think just um kind of finishing the plays right, especially when you talk about getting in the red zone, finishing and finding a way to uh get six points instead of three, right? Which obviously Spencer's been doing a great job of of keeping us, you know, getting points, but we want to, you know, get six as an offense and then uh but yeah, I think it just comes down to us finding a way and finishing. >> Kind of a simple question, but I know the scheduling is out of your control, but does it just kind of feel like it's been almost a month since you played a game at home? It just feels like it's been forever. >> Yeah, I think with the international trip in between some home games it's felt like a while, so it'll be good to get back in Louisville. >> Playing against the winless Titans team this week, you guys have had success against them recently, but what's the mentality heading into this with still being a division game? >> I mean, anytime you're playing, you know, a team in the NFL, it's it's a lot of good players over there and I don't think their record really is something you look at. It's a really good team and they got a good defense, so it's going to be a, you know, a big challenge to make sure we're we're on our stuff this week. >> You mentioned that defense. They're off They are pretty good. What did they do right in terms of limiting offense? >> Uh they've done a good job in the run game, obviously. I think those those stick out and then they've just got a lot of good players, some good, you know, front seven linebackers playing well, so they've been doing a lot of good stuff. >> Going back a few days, but Mo obviously played his 100th consecutive game. How much is that just a testament to his durability, the relentlessness for him to achieve that milestone and the standard that he sets for you guys as tight ends? >> Yeah, I think to, you know, have a guy like that in the room is is awesome for me as a a younger player and, you know, think about 100 games in a row is hard to even imagine right now after >> [laughter] >> playing not even 2 years yet, but but yeah, that's impressive for him to be doing that and and he has more than just 100 games. That was just in a row, which is the the crazy part. But yeah, it's cool to see. >> What's the most valuable lesson or, you know, element that you have learned from Mo in the time you've had to with him? >> Um I think he's a a very consistent, you know, person and player. Every day he shows up, he's got the same attitude and on the field I'd say he's the same player, too. So, kind of just his consistency in in whatever it is he's doing. >> Quenton Nelson said after the game on Sunday that everyone is capable of more in the run game. What do you think needs to change to get JT going a little bit more? >> Um I think just trusting ourselves. We've got a good good O-line and good tight ends and obviously JT's really good, so so sticking to what what's worked and not trying to do, you know, too much. Just do your job on each run play. >> You're going to play a team that's 0 and 5, yet they're not they're strong defensively. What about them is is is effective when you're scouting tape? >> Yeah, they got a good DC, um Saleh, and they got good players, so they they stay sound to their assignments and, you know, they got a good D-line up front. Starts with Simmons, he's a good player, so. >> That said, how important is it to keep a down team down? >> Uh I mean, wouldn't say it like that. I mean, division game, so it's important to win. Yeah. >> Looking at some of the red zone struggles over, specifically last week, what are some of the things that you wanted to see maybe executed better overall as an offense? >> You know, just punch it in instead of kicking field goals. I mean, we got to execute better and just starts with everybody taking care of their their job and that's that. I mean, credit to the Steelers, they they did their job, but we got to we got to be better. >> Teams are kind of watching out for you. They're targeting you. How do you How do you get those those more catches and more receptions in situations when they're gunning for you? >> Oh, yeah, man. You know, just opens up stuff for other players to make some plays, and you know, just got to do my assignment to the best of my ability, and that's all I can control.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, C.J. Stroud, and Marvin Harrison Jr. address the media
text: first acclimated and just what do you think? >> I thought Marvin did a really good job today getting acclimated. Our coaches did a great job, you know, in the in the background just really working with him, getting him caught up to speed on, you know, our plays, the verbiage of what we're doing. He got in, ran some plays today. Did a good job. The Jaguars are obviously off to a really good start. What have you seen from them that you think has contributed to how well they're doing? >> I think the the thing that sticks out to me about the Jaguars is the their play style. It jumps off the tape. Defensively, they're flying around. They're they're causing havoc. They do multiple things, moving their front well, pressuring, they they do a good job of just mixing it up. And then offensively, they're they're winning on third downs. And that's been the key for them. They stay on the field, they sustain drives because they they keep the third downs at a manageable uh area in that short window and they're able to have their whole playbook at their disposal. So, they're doing a good job. Liam has done a great job of leading that team for the second year in a row and they're they're off to a great start >> because CJ CJ obviously off to a great to a great start. But when it comes to like how he's been handling all the the pressure week in and week out and delivering, getting rid of the ball, go looking downfield, what have you seen the growth in that part of his game so far this year? >> The growth I've seen for CJ is just it he's confident when he's standing there. He gains that confidence by the pocket that he's able to have with our O line and doing a good job of protecting him, allowing him to make those good decisions, allow him to dish the football out to a lot of different guys. What are some of the things that a player has to go through? Like Marvin Harrison Jr. coming here is so late with you all already have gone through training camp five weeks into the season. How hard is it to get him caught up to speed? Brought up to speed, excuse me. >> You know, getting a player caught up. It isn't hard when the player is, you know, attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down. So, Marvin's first night here, he was with our assistant wide receiver coach, uh, Coach Taekwon, and they were grinding. and they were working late at night and they were they were in the playbook grinding and that allowed him, you know, to get a day ahead and now he was able to go out there today and just fit right in seamlessly. So when you put the work in and you're dialed in, you can make it work and >> it goes right into what CJ was saying about how hard Marvin is as a as a worker. >> It fits right in with everything I heard about him. He's been he's a hard worker. Hard worker. That's what that was the message that kept reverberating as we asked different people about him and it showed today at practice. He's lining up. He's not he's locked in on what we're asking to do. Getting the call, getting the line very easy. So, I'm excited to see how his uh his week continues to progress and see how much he can handle. >> Can you talk about any updates with guys like um Henry or Tank or any of the guys that have been injured? Hey, Henry was able to we were able to open Henry's window today, so he was able to get out and practice. Uh, so we're elated to have him back out at practice. Uh, and then Tank, he's Tank is still practicing. This his second week back at practice. He's looking looking really good. So, we'll continue to see how he progresses as the week goes on. >> Nick said that um, you know, I agree with that part, [snorts] but he added that he he thinks he could probably come back within the next two weeks. What will be the factors that will go into um deciding uh whether to activate? >> We'll keep allowing Tank to get as comfortable as he needs to be, right? Just giving him that time to get back to football because it's been such a long time since he was able to do, you know, a lot of team drills, put the pads on. So, he's working him way he's working himself back, you know, very well. He's he's looking fast. He's making decisive cuts. He's doing a really good job. So, we'll see how that timeline works. We know we opened up his window last week. We have 21 days to make that decision. So, we'll see where he is as we keep progressing. >> Have you decided if uh Marvin is going to play this week in London? >> Marvin will play. >> Have you How valuable do you think it is for you guys to have two receivers the size of Nico and and Marvin on your team? >> And to have two receivers, looking at both of them today, I'm like, man, those are two tough guys to cover. You got big, you know, tall receivers, right? You talk about the thing that separates those guys is their catch radius, right? Being tall, long guys, just when you put the ball up, they have that ability no matter where it is to kind of out jump a DB or really find a way to come down with those tough contested catches because of their size. So, they can utilize their size to, you know, body guys and get open and just play physical. So, I'm excited to see both guys out there on the field together. >> Are there any particular people you've leaned on to get ready for this um trip to London? maybe people who've been been there done that that kind of thing. >> The person I leaned on is person here in our building, our assistant head coach Danny Barrett. He was here when Texans went in 2019. So went through that schedule of what they were able to do, how he felt about, you know, the flow of everything and how it worked. So I've been leaning on coach Barry. He's been, you know, great mentor for me and God I can lean on and ask any questions. So we're we're dialed in. We're ready to roll. How much of a disadvantage is to play a team that has been in that time zone for more than a week and you guys have to adjust? >> I don't know what that advantage is or if there is an advantage. Um, my mindset and everything I'm telling our guys is when the ball is kicked off, like everybody wants to talk about the difference with the travel, the different with the timing and schedule. I want to talk about when the ball is kicked off, what are we doing? And that's what matters most to me. Let's allow Parker Washington to kind of grow into the player that they use him as now and how dynamic he's been both on offense and they use him on special teams. >> Parker Parker has been very dynamic. He literally he jumps off the tape with I mean he's playing explosive fast guy. We knew the type of returner he was, but now he's showing that skill set as a receiver and they're featuring him more. Uh he's more of the first guy in the progression and he's able to get open. He's playing fast. looks like he plays whatever speed he runs, he runs that speed every time he gets a route. So, he's a guy who's made some tough catches. He's a tough player, you know, kind of a late round guy who's really made a name for himself just by I see a a guy who really works at his craft and he's gotten better at playing receiver. He's a dynamic returner as we all know and you know, that's the primary guy for us defensively that we have to try to stop. What's kind of that process of figuring out, you know, obviously Marvin's going to play this week, so it's kind of that process of figuring out what works well for him, what doesn't work well for him in a short period of time to make sure that he can still, as you always like to say, play fast. >> It's when uh when you get a player like to come in late as Marvin has, it's just again like what is what is he able to pick up on? We go through the entire playbook. will have set plays and we'll make sure it's as easy as possible for him to get lined up so he can play fast. Don't expect him to come out and play, you know, all 60 snaps in the game, but we'll make sure he gets what he needs and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do. >> Defense continue to build on what will that you want to build on and what do you still think y'all need to fix? >> Defensively, the thing that went well for us is, you know, we got off the field on third down. We took the football away and you know we we stopped the run and that formula it really doesn't change. We didn't give up many explosive passes. That was something that was hurting us the first couple weeks and when you limit the explosive plays that you give up, you limit the points that go on the board. Our guys know that. We know that's our formula. We got to keep the ball in front of us. We got to go tackle well and we have to lean on that. Again, the formula, it doesn't change to me no matter who you're playing. Like there is a style that you need. You got to keep the ball in front of you and you got to get off the field on third down and all those critical situations, third down and red zone. >> I'll go ahead. >> You guys wanted to run [snorts] the ball more this season successfully than you guys obviously have. What can you say about Nick's ability to adapt and change into what the offense is now and how has he grown as a play caller and game planner? And Nick has done a great job is, you know, one thing I really like about Nick Kaye with how he calls the game and what he can call just his ability to go in and out of different play play styles, right? Not for the 49ers, not for the commanders. A lot of people asking about Christian Kirk. Well, the issue with Christian Kirk is the calf and it's been an issue for months for Christian Kirk. title: Bucky Irving on Motivating the Offense | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Uh I always say it starts with the guys up front. And when them guys come to play, they're one of the best in the league and I trust them guys. You know, we go out there and go into war on Sundays. Uh I feel like they're the best in the game when they when they come to play. So, just being able to to be on the same page with them guys I'll say just trust in my track. And when I trust my track, good things happen. >> You always bring a lot of energy, but it looked like you're firing those guys in front up before the game a little bit. What what was going on with those conversations? Is it just something you do every Sunday or every Thursday night? >> No, you know, I'm I'm more of a guy that been in the back don't really say too much. I I just try to lead by example not really uh talking too much, but uh I was just just tired of losing, bro. And and them guys it starts with them guys up front. I mean, they set the tone however the game going to go, however they come out, however they feeling. Uh it starts in practice. So, I tell them guys it starts in practice and it translates to the game. So, just being able to to trust them guys up front and get it going. And if they keep rolling, we going to keep rolling. >> Can you describe that run because there didn't seem to be a lot there and your patience and then you just kind of picked your way through and all of a sudden you're running 20 miles an hour. >> Uh when I when I got the ball, I had to make a move in the backfield, but I originally got back to where I was supposed to hit at and then pretty much let my instincts and my ability to kick in and then I kind of got through that and I seen daylight and I tried I tried I tried to go all the way, but I ran out of gas. >> Okay, what was the reaction from the skip people in the film room to that play? Specifically, what did he say? >> Uh it's not really no reaction. He know that we are capable of making them plays in the room. So, it's not really a big deal. Uh we watched the film, put it to bed, and then moved on to Pittsburgh. So. >> What did it mean to you to be the one to close out the game as well with that run that sealed the deal for that win? >> Uh it wasn't me. It was the guys blocking it. I never give credit for what I do is always the guys that's blocking for me. They get all the credit uh because them guys are the ones that's opening up the lanes and I just got to do my do my job at a high level and trust my technique and good things happen. >> Thank you. I mean like I said it starts them guys up front and you seeing it just the extra strain by Ben Bence. I mean he bring it every week so just being able to know that them guys going to strain and like I always say it takes all 11 in the run game. Everyone got to strain through the whistle cuz you never know I probably cut it back to your side I probably go the other way just but just being able to know that you got that type of guy back there that's running the football and just being able to strain through the whistle. I mean we won't look at that type of stuff. We take it game by game and we got to go out here and prepare for the Pittsburgh Steelers. We got a good football team coming in here so just being able to to stay focused stay on the course and take it one game at a time. Uh Sometimes you got to you got to come out to shell a little bit and just being able to know that I can fire them guys up and and and knowing that when I do say something it means a little something cuz I don't I don't say a lot so just being able to know that I mean don't nobody like losing. I mean if you're competitive no one's like losing so just being able to know when I say something it means a lot to the guys and just being able to go out there and execute at a high level. Oh yeah yeah he actually called me and thanked me for for shouting him out on the TV so you know that's my guy I'm always staying in contact with him. Death by inches you know what it is death by inches you got to stay in your routine you can't can't get satisfied with the results that you had. Give yourself a 24-hour rule and move on. >> You're still there 5 something >> Every day, bro. I don't change. >> Anything else? >> Thank you, Bobby. Appreciate it. >> Yeah.

They do a great job of of playing them both and then subbing them out doing different things with those guys. Both can run with the ball afterwards. Both are very good blockers. So, you know, other than the receivers, they present a great challenge as well. >> Just curious what you've seen from Keonte Scott as he kind of grows within his game. >> Keith's been one of our best players this year. Wants to be good, wants to be great, extremely tough, puts in the work during the week and that's what you really like about him. What has been the secret to that success for no matter if it's a safety coming in playing that or a quarterback coming in playing that that that position has really shined for you during their rookie seasons? >> Just their knowledge of the game and you can't just grab a corner and throw him in there and play nickel because he can cover. You got to have a certain mindset to play in there. And we've been good enough to draft those guys to have those guys that can go in there and do other things. And you know it it's been you want to keep one in there but like I said they all graduate to starters and you can't keep them in there enough. So the fact that all of them have played on the field and played nickel at one point or another they don't panic and they cover for each other when somebody messes up the other ones say okay I can do this you do that and that that helps us out a lot as far as the versatility is concerned. So you know that that's a very very unique position to play in today's game. Curry started last year outside for you a few a few games a number of games. But his work ethic, his quickness, his understanding of route combinations of what you try to do to him and he just loves to compete. He doesn't say much, but he loves to compete and he's the same guy every day, and you can appreciate that about him. >> Todd, every week seems head coaches, uh, they're under scrutiny for late game decisions. You know, some fans want guys fired after for one bad decision. Sometimes you enter the arena of sports, no matter what field you're in, you win, you get cheered, you lose, you get booed. That kind of comes with it. You lean on people that's been with you a while. You lean on the information you get from up top. You lean on experience. You lean on all kind of things how your team is playing. text: Always a pleasure to welcome back to the program head coach of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. It's Marcus Freeman. I would always say thank you for the time but given that you got a big game coming up Saturday night particularly appreciate it. So, thank you. >> Absolutely. Thanks for having me, Scott. >> Always. I saw you this summer at Jordan Cornett Cornett's wonderful charity function and I said we'll see you in the playoff. Nothing's changed my mind. You played six games. But as you look at these six games and what you all have done, what are you most pleased with collectively? >> You know, I think the the easy thing to say is the the execution and and you know, how they played overall. But for me it's the preparation and the way they prepared during the week. Um the intentionality, uh the physicality in practice, but also the intentionality outside of practice and the way they've been able to take care of their bodies, prepare mentally. Um all those things are really was what has equated to some of the success that we're having. >> There was a game in the rain in Chapel Hill where it was one point in the second half for a moment. But largely largely coach, you've not been stressed in the fourth quarter. Huge game on the road against a BYU team that's top 10 as well. What challenges are you preparing your group for this week that perhaps you've not encountered yet? >> Yeah, I think look every game presents its own challenges and there's been challenging situations um all season long that that maybe the person that looks at the outcome doesn't see. Uh but there there definitely are. Um and so it is as this one comes there we know it's going to be a hostile environment. Um we're going to a place that many people in this program have never been. Um and we're going to face an extremely talented and well-coached uh football team. And so they do some unique things on both sides of the ball and uh we're going to have to handle whatever they give us and be able to communicate and then and go out and make the adjustments that are necessary to have success. >> CJ Carr's numbers pop, 16 touchdowns, only one pick. What's the clearest indication to you, Marcus, of growth year over year in your quarterback? >> I think the to only have one turnover in these six games with uh the amount of opportunities that we we've thrown the ball, it speaks volumes of his decision-making and his ball placement and some of the other things that I really think he does well that people may not see is the ability to keep our offense out of negative situations. To see what a defense is doing and check a run or check the protection and and really make sure our offense is in a favorable position is a huge advantage for us and and somewhere it's an area of growth. Like we have captains, two on offense, two on defense and those guys are amazing.
