But, I love the way that he played this weekend. And that to me is how he's got to play. Is get back, rip it, push the ball down the field, do those things that you did so well last year. And he finally did that for a whole game this past weekend. >> And the rip it, just keep ripping it. Just see it, rip it. Don't don't think about it. Just play like yourself. Be instinctive is the conversation going on right now in Denver. Um that's what Bo Nix said in his media availability on Tuesday cuz they're playing Thursday to kick off week six against Seattle. My goodness, what a great game that's going to be with so much on the line already just 1/3 into the season. Uh anything that you saw differently with Sean Payton calling the plays in Bo Nix, Kurt? >> No, not really. I mean they they struggled offensively again. You know, I just and I get a lot of it to me falls to Bo Nix just in terms of patience in the pocket. Um you know, I've seen it for years. It continues to be there. At some point it's like, okay, how do we fix this? How do we fix this problem? And there were a number of times again this past weekend where he hits the top of his drop and he's moving already. And it's before things even develop in the play concept gives him, you know, a chance to see what's there and and make the plays that are in front of him. And you know, I don't know what the issue is because it's been going on so long. You know, and again I I remember asking Sean Payton about it last year in one of our production meetings. And you know, he kind of just gave us the answer that, well, that's kind of who Bo Nix is. He feels more comfortable with his feet moving. And okay, that's great. But if you continue to miss opportunity after opportunity because that's happening, something has to change. And at some point he's got to, you know, figure that out. Figure that piece out of it where he can get back to his drop or time his drop better so he can see what's going on and take, you know, some of these layups or some of these plays that are right within structure. You know, that that you're just not going to be able to live in this hit the back foot run around and think you're going to create plays for 60 minutes every week to win games. You've got to allow the system and the playmakers around you to make plays for you. And you know, this has been a consistent thing throughout his career. The ironic thing is that when we get into late game situations and he's got to make plays, he's shown that he can do it. He's shown that he can make all the throws and and make those reads and do those things. It's just why why is it not happening early in games? Why is there more of a panic early in games? You know, of course he's forced into it in the fourth quarter, but knowing he could play like that and having played like that in some moments, it just it's kind of dumbfounding that this continues to be the issue with him in in my opinion. >> And then watching that film for the Chargers, what would you counsel the Chargers to do to fix things and change things offensively? And I understand that could be a radical choice. Curt. But what would you counsel Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers to do now at 0-5? >> I I would just counsel them to get back to the base. Like Mike McDaniel's been very innovative with his offenses and what he's trying to do and all the motions and shifts and and creating, you know, certain opportunities for throws. And you know, when I watch the film, there's a lot of times that, you know, I'm scratching my head going, "What are we trying to do here?" And I almost feel sometimes like it's, "Hey, we're going to just try something that's really kind of off-the-wall and different because we've got Justin Herbert who can do it or, you know, we think that if we do this, the defense is going to do that and it's going to look like a a really good play cuz we're doing something different than everybody else is doing. And a lot of it to me doesn't make sense. It doesn't add up or it's not playing out the way that they must think it's going to play out. And for me, it would just be like, "All right, let's go back to some basic football. Some Jim Harbaugh going to line up and we're going to run these runs. We're not going to try to fool anybody or we're not going to necessarily over motion and and and hope we can get the defense out of position. Let's just play some more smash mouth, you know, real football and say, "Hey, we're going to beat you whether you know what we're doing or not. We're going to beat you by our physicality and our play making." And then do the same thing in the pass game. Is get back to some of those concepts that um that Justin Herbert has done well, uh that that, you know, just kind of staple concepts that you see around the league each and every week and see if that can, you know, settle things down and cause you to play more consistent football, um you know, on both ends. Cuz to me, there's just so many negative plays when you watch them, um you know, when you watch a course of a game is that there's just so much chaos going on that it's hard to be consistent uh if you're not staying on schedule and you're not, you know, just making some consistent plays. And one play might be all right, then the next play you're losing yards and it's negatives and it's not working out. And uh to me, it's just a lot of chaos right now. And I would just go, "Okay, we're going to scrap some of all that stuff. We can come back to it at some point. Let's, you know, figure out what our identity is and what our base is, what we can live off of, and then we can start stacking things once we show some consistency in those areas." >> Now, look, I'm sure it's not helpful that Rashawn Slater, Joe Walt, Lad McConkey, and Quentin Johnston are out. That's what happened against the Broncos. So, I understand that there's less than than what they're used to having for Justin Herbert to throw to. But, is it fair to say that what Mike McDaniel was brought in to do is something that Justin Herbert either is uncomfortable doing or just simply cannot do? And that's the ultimate problem. Is that fair to ask? >> Uh I mean, I think it's fair to ask and I think it could be um it could be true. And again, the one thing I don't want to do here is just kind of throw all this on Justin Herbert and say, "Oh, well, you know, Justin can't do it, but everybody else could do it." I've been very outspoken that what Mike McDaniels does in an offense is unique, and it takes a unique type of quarterback to really fit into, and specifically I'm going back to to Miami because I'm not fully sure what they are in in in LA yet. But going back to Miami, that it takes a specific quarterback to do those things. And Tua was actually a really good fit when he was playing good football, and that's why he led the National Football League in in passing one year. But that anticipation, the ability to have touch, the ability to turn and see and understand spacing quickly is a rare thing. I I don't think there's a lot of quarterbacks in the National Football League that would be great at that. And so, I know we're going to look at this specific situation and go, "Oh, Justin Herbert can't do that. Whatever. He's not as good as we thought." I think there's a lot of quarterbacks that would struggle in that system. And so, that becomes the interesting dynamic is you brought him in maybe to do some of that stuff, but if Justin is one of those quarterbacks that wouldn't thrive in that type of system, now what are we going to do? You know, how are we going to figure this out so we get Justin playing at his best, but we also get the best of Mike McDaniel and and and the and the creativity and the uniqueness of their offense. But right now, it doesn't seem like we have either. The other you Mike McDaniel isn't like creating these easy what I call layups, high hoppers for his quarterback. And then Justin doesn't look comfortable playing within what they're asking him to do. Um, you know, and I'll even say another thing cuz I talk about it a lot. This whole idea of pure progression versus, you know, full field coverage-based read type stuff. And I believe that Justin Herbert has been more in the world of the coverage-based reads. And there, you know, what Miami has done and that system has been more pure progression. Okay, what what does that have to do with anything? Well, I I think a big part of the pure progression is coaches telling quarterbacks to see if their receiver is open. Okay, so you come back and you're looking at your guy to determine can I throw it to my guy? In a coverage-based or full-field type read offense, I'm coming back and looking at defenders. And those defenders will tell me if that guy is open or not. Now again, this is all speculation here, but when I watched Justin Herbert the last couple weeks drop back and throw the ball right to a defender like numerous times. Like we're all looking at these plays going what is he looking at? Like how could he not see that defender that's right where he threw it like he hit him in the numbers. And I wonder sometimes if that's Justin not focusing on defenders and looking at his receiver and going okay, I got to make this throw to the receiver and all of a sudden as he's making the throw the defender sitting right there because he's not focusing on defenders and he's focusing on his receivers. Again, speculation, but I've seen it a lot in pure progression offenses where guys are looking at their guys as opposed to the opposing team's guys and they're a bit oblivious, right? Cuz anything that we do, if you focus on one thing you might be able to feel what's outside of, you know, that focus, but you don't fully know. If you're focusing on something else, then, you know, you have the chance and that's what I mean by focusing on the defenders, you have a chance to truly see where they're at and dictate whether we make a different throw or whether we throw it to somebody else. And so that's some of the speculation that I I have and I wonder because I know kind of the nature of pure progression type systems and if that's something that may be messing with Justin Herbert as he's coming back and trying to find his guy and throw it to him and complete it to him and he's losing sight of the bigger picture and and what defenders are doing and it's why we're seeing some of these kind of crazy interceptions that we've seen from him the last couple weeks. Man. Wow. That's the only way I can respond to that. Um so even if Justin Herbert in this offense leads the league through five weeks in to use a word that you just used obliviousness and plays where it makes people go how did that happen? >> Yeah. >> For one hot second the Washington Commanders took that mantle. >> And if you will blew a win with it. What do you think happened at the end of the Commanders Giants game from your seat in London watching it back Kirk? >> The only thing that I can imagine happened there was in that moment um Jayden wasn't given all the information in that moment. Um you know in terms of no timeouts, we're calling a pass play. This is what we're trying to do, right? Like we don't have time to throw it incomplete in bounds. It's got to be a throw to the sideline. If it's not there, throw it away, stop the clock for like that he wasn't given all the information in that moment. You know, even if he was given the information earlier in a drive or or going out on the field or whatever, um that in that moment, you know, there was just a lot going on and he didn't have all the information that he needed to make the That's the only thing I can imagine. You know, again, Jayden could have got the information and as he dropped back to pass and things got messed up a little bit, he lost, you know, he lost sight of all of that stuff and decided to run and then realized that he made like that's possible. But I I I really feel like you see this all the time and in kind of two-minute situations is that, you know, a play is called where you know you have to get out of bounds. So everything is called to the sideline and you drop back as a quarterback and you peek at it but you know the defense is covering the sideline and, you know, your thought process is, "Hey, if it pops open now, throw it. If not, just wing this thing out of bounds cuz you understand that scenario in a game. At the end of, you know, a half or at the end of a game that, "Hey, they're probably going to take this away but we're going to call it. If we get an easy one to get us 5 yards and get closer for the field goal, take it. If not, launch it into the stands and we live for another day." And so that's the scenario that, you know, we've seen play out a million times. And so that's what makes me think somewhere in that communication, in that moment, Jayden didn't get all of that information. >> Yeah, I know. But except Chris Paul, the offensive guard for the Commanders said they talked about it in the huddle. >> In the huddle. Okay, I didn't hear that one. Sorry about that. >> but I know what it looks like from afar and that's why I asked you. You can you you obviously we don't know. But he said they talked about it in the huddle. >> They talked about the fact that they had no time outs. >> Correct. Correct. Correct. The the exact exchange, just so you're aware, he was asked, "Was it talked Did they Did they know any time outs that they had no time outs left in the final drive of overtime?" Chris Paul said, quote unquote, "Yes, that was talked about in the huddle." End quote. >> In the huddle. >> And so And so my question as well is cuz it took me a honestly, it took me a while to watch it back. Cuz the way I described it on Monday show, it was like a horror movie. Like you you see the [laughter] the guy in the chainsaw is standing there, you know, move faster. Um and and it was tough to watch back but I I did and then I watched it over and over again. It looks like Daniels gets stepped on by one of his linemen coming out, and it threw something off, and maybe he Last time that happened, you know, his his left arm folded like an accordion. So, I don't know. He kind of lost himself is what it looked like right there. >> Very easily. I mean, we've all we've all had that happen, and I'm with you. I you know, I just saw a couple replays, and I thought something funky happened, too, when he was coming out from under center like he you know, fumbled with the ball a little bit, or as you said, I didn't see him get stepped on, but that could have very easily been it as well. And and you know, we've all been there where something happens, and it throws our whole entire thought process off of what we were thinking, you know, 2 seconds before that. You know, and you would have thought in that moment just in his head was >> Third and >> Hey, it's a completion or a throwaway. >> So, as soon as something went wrong, it's it's turn and throw it. But, you know, is there another scenario where in that moment because it's he's like, I'm in the pocket. What if I just turn and whip it, you know, out of bounds, you know, you know, without even thinking about it, you know, is there a penalty here? And all of a sudden now I get a grounding call because I'm in the pocket >> Right. >> There's a there's a lot of things that come up in the course of, you know, 2 or 3 seconds like that that you have to think about and consider. Um and and again, I don't know, you know, nobody's going to know except Jayden specifically what really happened in the moment. And it might have been just like you said, he had everything in his mind, this is what I'm going to do, and then all of a sudden he gets stepped on, he thinks he's going to stumble, maybe going to, you know, fall and take a sack. >> What am I going to do? And now all of a sudden he just loses his wits and and makes a play that that he's going to regret. >> And then essentially takes a sack. He sacks himself. >> Yep. >> I still it still blows my mind. Um I got 60 seconds left. Quarterback that looked best on on tape week eight week five to you is which? >> Jordan Love. Um you know, who hasn't necessarily looked great. Their team hasn't looked great, but >> [laughter] >> against the Bears, he looked incredible. I mean, you just watch the tape and it's just bombs away. He's just winging the ball all over down the field and making plays. He was He was awesome this weekend. I thought he was the best quarterback that was out there. >> And did they solve their offensive woes with protection in the run game by just just throwing it deep or just or they just knew that the Bears were susceptible and and you know, with this rivalry the floors like just keep just keep hitting them hard. >> I mean, it was one of those things that a lot of the plays weren't really perfectly designed. I mean, he just threw it up against the coverage and said, "Show me you're going to cover it." You know, the one deep post where Theineman's back there and you know, his guy makes a play. They got another cover two look where he just throws a go route down the sideline. That safety should be there to make a play and the safety squats and he just runs right by the safety. So, it was just to me it was like a perfect storm. Everything went wrong for Chicago. Everything went right for Green Bay. I'm not ready to say, "Oh, you know, Chicago should panic and Green Bay's got you know, everything put back together." This was one game where it just seemed to be out of whack from the get-go and we'll see where it takes these two teams moving forward. But, I'm just not ready to you know, say, "Green Bay's solved all their issues just because you know, they got you know, five or six huge plays in that game that that you know, that that got you know, took it away from Chicago very early. >> Kurt, you're the man. We'll chat again. We'll see you soon. Sorry about the internet issue. >> No, it's all good. >> Kurt Warner, everybody. >> We connected just like Jordan Love with all of his receivers.
